title: D. Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap

legend: You are given n%%ZSMJ0%% pairs of integers (a1,b1),(a2,b2),…,(an,bn)%%ZSMJ1%%. All of the integers in the pairs are distinct and are in the range from 1%%ZSMJ2%% to 2⋅n%%ZSMJ3%% inclusive.
Let's call a sequence of integers x1,x2,…,x2k%%ZSMJ4%% good if either

You need to choose a subset of distinct indices i1,i2,…,it%%ZSMJ7%% and their order in a way that if you write down all numbers from the pairs in a single sequence (the sequence would be ai1,bi1,ai2,bi2,…,ait,bit%%ZSMJ8%%), this sequence is good.
What is the largest subset of indices you can choose? You also need to construct the corresponding index sequence i1,i2,…,it%%ZSMJ9%%.
input: The first line contains single integer n%%ZSMJ10%% (2≤n≤3⋅105%%ZSMJ11%%) — the number of pairs.
Each of the next n%%ZSMJ12%% lines contain two numbers — ai%%ZSMJ13%% and bi%%ZSMJ14%% (1≤ai,bi≤2⋅n%%ZSMJ15%%) — the elements of the pairs.
It is guaranteed that all integers in the pairs are distinct, that is, every integer from 1%%ZSMJ16%% to 2⋅n%%ZSMJ17%% is mentioned exactly once.
output: In the first line print a single integer t%%ZSMJ18%% — the number of pairs in the answer.
Then print t%%ZSMJ19%% distinct integers i1,i2,…,it%%ZSMJ20%% — the indexes of pairs in the corresponding order.
note: The final sequence in the first example is 1<7>3<5>2<10%%ZSMJ21%%.
The final sequence in the second example is 6>1<3>2<5>4%%ZSMJ22%%.
